---
title: "generate-random-password"
description: "Generate a random base64 or numeric-only password from /dev/urandom"
---

## Overview

`generate-random-password` generates a random string of a specified length
using `/dev/urandom`. Useful for passwords, tokens, or test data.

- **Default** — base64 characters (alphanumeric + `/` + `+`)
- **`-n`** — numeric-only digits

```bash
$ generate-random-password
X7kP2mRqLsT8nH0w

$ generate-random-password -n 8
49302817
```

## Dependencies

- `/dev/urandom`
- `base64`, `tr` — standard POSIX tools

## Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-n` | Generate a numeric-only string |
| `-h` | Show help and exit. |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `[length]` | Length of the output string (default: `16`, max: `76`) |

## Usage

```bash
# Default — 16-char base64
generate-random-password

# 32-char base64
generate-random-password 32

# 8-char numeric
generate-random-password -n 8

# Length before or after flag
generate-random-password 12 -n
generate-random-password -n 12
```

## Notes

- Maximum length is 76 (one less than 77, which is rejected by the validator).
- The length must be a positive integer greater than 0.
